mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificado de homónimos (Name clearance certificate issued by Cámara de Comercio)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (Bogota Chamber of Commerce)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for use outside Colombia) OR domestic notary recognition for internal filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Pasaporte o identificación oficial del accionista extranjero (Certified copy of foreign shareholder passport or government-issued ID)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and registered translation into Spanish where applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Poder especial (Special power of attorney for pre-incorporation formalities)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Colombian Notary 1 Envigado or Notary of the chosen domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization only; if executed abroad, Hague Apostille and certified Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificado de existencia y representación legal de la sociedad extranjera matriz (Certificate of existence and legal representation of foreign corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies house or registry of foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and certified Spanish translation (or consular legalization if foreign jurisdiction is not a Hague member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Declaración de beneficiario final de la persona jurídica sujeta a constitución (UBO declaration for the Colombian S.A.S. to be incorporated)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Colombian Notary and subsequently DIAN (RUBF filing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization and electronic filing with DIAN

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, and direct UBOs against the UIAFListasVinculantes (binding Colombian lists), the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) SDN list, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, and any national preventive measures under Law 526 of 1999. A risk-based customer due diligence file must be maintained covering the commercial purpose, source of funds, and beneficial ownership chain. For a low-risk designer toy merchandising company under ISIC 3240, enhanced due diligence is not automatically triggered unless any individual appears on a sanctions or PEP list or anomalies are identified in the transaction rationale.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES - Registro Único Empresarial y Social (www.rues.org.co) and the online platform of the Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (ccb.org.co)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in the Spanish language or in a Spanish-transliterated form useable in Colombian commerce. The name must include 'S.A.S.' or 'Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada' as the corporate form indicator. Foreign brand names, designer collectible lines, and English-language trademarks may be registered only with prior trademark or IP clearance and must be transliterated according to Spanish pronunciation and orthographic rules when incorporated into the corporate name. Special signs, symbols, or non-Latin characters are generally prohibited in the corporate name field.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Ministerio de Hacienda y Crédito Público
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name clearance rejection, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration petition (recurso de reposición) before the same Cámara de Comercio registry authority within ten (10) business days of notification. The motion must clearly identify the proposed name, the grounds of rejection, evidence of the distinctiveness of the name, and any trademark or IP registration certificate supporting the requested name. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may lodge an appeal (recurso de apelación) before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) through the chamber registry office within five (5) business days. The chamber must transmit the complete administrative file to the SIC for resolution. During the appeal process, a new name reservation cannot be filed for the same corporate object, but the applicant may simultaneously initiate a secondary name reservation application for a contingency name if urgent incorporation is required. The final resolution of the appeal is binding on the chamber and the requesting party.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are permitted for the purpose of receiving statutory notices and meeting the Cámara de Comercio registered domicile requirement, provided the arrangement is contracted with a licensed corporate services provider operating within the same municipality and the physical location serves as a valid administrative address. The business activity (designer toy merchandising under ISIC 3240) does not expressly require physical production or warehousing premises in Colombia for registration purposes; however, the registered office must correspond to the jurisdiction where the principal commercial and administrative functions are exercised. The UBO and PEP profile must reflect the actual control and decision-making location of the entity. The virtual office must not be a mere mail-forwarding address if the company substantially operates in Colombia; otherwise it may be considered a sham domicile by the Superintendencia de Sociedades.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Arts. 1, 4, 5, 17-22; Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971), Arts. 110-117, 373, 375; Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015, Book 4; Ley 1780 de 2016 (Fast S.A.S. provisions)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) acting through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) and the Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE) electronic portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución de S.A.S. (private incorporation deed with full bylaws), authenticated by the Chamber of Commerce; elevated to public deed before a notary only when real estate is contributed to the share capital
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital applies to S.A.S. entities; the incorporating shareholder freely fixes subscribed and paid-up capital, and any deferred installment subscriptions must be fully paid within two years from incorporation (Art. 4, Ley 1258 de 2008). No escrow account is mandated; paid-in funds may be deposited directly to the corporate bank account, and registration taxes (Impuesto de Registro at 0.7% of subscribed capital) must be settled before the Chamber issues the certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: CORPORATE ACT NO. 1 OF [DATE] – INCORPORATING SHAREHOLDER OF [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S. 1) The Founder subscribes the entire authorized share capital, [COP P] paid as capital stock, pursuant to the S.A.S. law. 2) The registered office is fixed at the declared address in Bogotá D.C. 3) The appointment of [Sole Manager] as legal representative and administrator is ratified, including powers to represent, sign contracts, and register the company. 4) The legal representative is instructed to complete the RUES filing, obtain NIT/RUT, open corporate bank accounts, and procure all permits required to commence manufacturing of designer blind box toys. 5) Share capital funds may be remitted and used solely for corporate formation costs until the company is formally registered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name availability check and homonymy certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá / RUES — online name-search module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the proposed razón social through the Chamber's 'Verificación de similitud de nombres' tool and reserve the selected name for up to 30 days. The system issues a Certificado de Homonimia confirming that no identical or confusingly similar corporate name is registered.
required_dossiers: Application form for name search
List of up to three alternative proposed names
Copy of the shareholder's identification document or passport
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for similarity, submit a revised name or obtain a written no-objection letter from the prior holder within the reservation window; a new search cycle may be opened without additional penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and authentication of the private incorporation document
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Única del Círculo (for public deed cases) or Cámara de Comercio for simple private-document authentication
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the S.A.S. bylaws including company name, domicile, corporate purpose covering ISIC 3240 designer toy manufacturing, share capital structure, management and legal representation, audit and conflict-of-interest rules, dissolution grounds and arbitration clause. Execute the private document among all incorporators; if a shareholder contributes real estate, elevate the document to a public deed before a notary.
required_dossiers: Draft bylaws (Estatutos Sociales)
Valid ID or passport of each incorporator
Certificado de Homonimia
Financial statements of contributing corporate shareholders where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any notarial or legal objections regarding capacity, prohibited clauses, or incomplete corporate purpose; re-execute the instrument within the 30-day authenticity term, or restart the execution with reformulated bylaws.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration with the Chamber of Commerce (Registro Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio / RUES / Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed incorporation instrument together with the RUES registration form and the legal representative's acceptance of office. The Chamber verifies payment of registration fees and the Impuesto de Registro, then issues the Certificado de Matrícula Mercantil and electronically transmits the corporate data to DIAN for provisional NIT assignment.
required_dossiers: Documento Privado de Constitución (or public deed)
RUES registration form signed by the legal representative
Legal representative acceptance of office
Certificado de Homonimia
Shareholders' identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUES filing is returned for omissions, correct the requested fields within the term indicated in the Chamber's ticket; provide clarifications on corporate purpose, capital payment schedule, or representative powers, and resubmit electronically without re-paying the registration fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive tax registration (NIT and RUT) before DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — RUT portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After commercial registration, DIAN assigns the definitive NIT; the legal representative must complete the RUT profile by adding the correct economic activities (ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930), selecting tax responsibilities (e.g., RA — IVA, RC — Industry and Commerce Tax, 06 — income and equity), and downloading the definitive RUT certificate. If exporting is intended, the company must subscribe to the exporter registration regime.
required_dossiers: Provisional NIT assigned by the Chamber
Identification document of the legal representative
Bylaws and commercial registration certificate
Bank account details (optional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN blocks the RUT due to data inconsistency, schedule a virtual appointment and correct the RUES–DIAN mismatch through the 'corrección con saneamiento' procedure; resubmit the form with certified accounts or additional explanatory documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer registration with social security, ARL and payroll systems
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administradora de Riesgos Laborales (ARL), EPS, AFP, Caja de Compensación Familiar — via Planilla Integrada de Liquidación de Aportes (PILA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the S.A.S. as an employer with a licensed ARL using the correct industrial classification for plastics and vinyl manufacturing (high-risk class IV/V), enroll the first employees in EPS and pension funds, and register the company with a Caja de Compensación Familiar. The employer must also adopt the Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SG-SST) for the manufacturing site.
required_dossiers: RUT and NIT certification
Commercial registration certificate
Legal representative ID
ARL enrollment form and labor risk classification
Initial SG-SST workplace assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ARL declines the registration due to industrial hazard classification, present a specific occupational risk assessment under NTC 4114; if contributions cannot be processed, correct the payroll data on PILA within the same working month to avoid surcharges.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance start-up: bank account, share ledger and UBO filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Regulated commercial banks and Cámara de Comercio / RUES (Beneficiarios Finales registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate demand deposit account with a regulated Colombian bank, comply with KYC/AML due diligence for a Standard Low-Risk legal entity, and transfer the paid-up share capital into the account. Then issue the subscribed shares, open the Libro de Registro de Acciones, and file the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (UBO declaration) before the Chamber of Commerce within two months of incorporation, as required by Law 2155 of 2021 and related regulations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and RUT/NIT
Identification and financial source declarations of the legal representative
Bank statement evidencing paid-up capital
UBO declaration form listing natural persons with control or 5%+ shareholding
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays onboarding for AML review, provide a certified extract of the bylaws and traceable source-of-funds documentation; UBO extension requests may be filed with a sworn statement of the ownership chain pending completion of the equivalent ownership mapping.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal zoning clearance, fire safety certificate and physical premises licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía Municipal / Secretaría de Planeación and Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Certificado de Uso de Suelo confirming that the industrial premises allow rotocasting and airbrush manufacturing, secure the Certificado de Bomberos after a fire-safety inspection (extinguishers, emergency exits, signage, evacuation drill plan), and verify structural load compliance under the NSR-10 seismic code for installed equipment and storage racks before commencing operations.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership title over the industrial premises
Floor plan with machinery and storage layout
RUT and commercial registration certificate
Fire-safety inspection form and SG-SST plan
Structural stamping certificate by a licensed architect or engineer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the zoning certificate rejects manufacturing use, appeal to the planning authority or seek a change of use permit; for fire deficiencies, correct the inspection findings within the stated ten-day term and reapply, submitting a revised stamped layout.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio, Industria y Turismo (MINCIT) and Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) — the latter enforces the Reglamento Técnico de Juguetes (Resolución 686 de 2018, incorporating ISO 8124 / NTC 5864 conformity standards) for market access of designer toys
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro de Productor / Fabricante de Juguetes ante la SIC, together with the municipal Registro de Funcionamiento Industrial y Comercial (Matrícula Mercantil con actividad industrial) and the Certificado de Conformidad Técnica de Producto (NTC-ISO 8124) issued by a SIC-accredited certification body

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) and the regional Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) of the jurisdiction (e.g., CAR Cundinamarca) or Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente for Bogotá D.C.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría II — Simplified Environmental Impact Declaration (Declaración de Cumplimiento Ambiental / Registro de Vertimientos y Emisiones Atmosféricas) under Decreto 1076 de 2015; a full Licencia Ambiental is not triggered unless the installed capacity, volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions, or hazardous waste generation exceeds the thresholds enumerated in Art. 2.2.2.3.2.2 of Decreto 1076 de 2015.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Airbrushing and rotocasting VOC emissions must comply with the atmospheric emission limits of Resolución 909 de 2008; industrial wastewater discharge must meet the parameters of Resolución 0631 de 2015 (pH 6.0–9.0, TSS ≤ 240 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 240 mg/L, and applicable priority pollutants) under a municipal sewer discharge permit; hazardous wastes (paints, solvents, vinyl scrap, contaminated PPE) must be handed to a licensed gestor de residuos peligrosos under Decreto 4741 de 2005 and Resolución 00528 de 2015, with quarterly manifests retained.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance via the Certificado de Bomberos covering extinguisher sizing, emergency exits, alarm systems and evacuation drills; structural load inspection and seismic-compliance stamping under NSR-10 for the production floor, mezzanines and storage racks; and workplace occupational clearance comprising ARL registration, a full SG-SST program, airbrush booth ventilation certification, and operational verification of occupational exposure limits for VOCs and particulate matter.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - Colombia's national tax and customs authority; principal portal www.dian.gov.co; e-filing and virtual transactions exclusively through the 'Muisca' platform (muisca.dian.gov.co).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon notarial execution of the S.A.S. bylaws: (1) register with the local Cámara de Comercio to obtain the 'Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal'; (2) complete the 'Inscripción al Registro Único Tributario (RUT)' through the Muisca portal or at a DIAN office, obtaining the NIT and automatically classifying the company as a 'Responsable del Régimen Común de IVA'; (3) appoint a legal representative with Colombian residency; (4) acquire a digital signature certificate from a DIAN-accredited certification authority (e.g., Certicámara or GSE); and (5) register the mandatory electronic invoicing obligation in the RUT and engage a DIAN-authorized billing software or technology operator. Standard processing: 8-20 business days including electronic-invoice enablement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The S.A.S. is a Colombian tax resident (Estatuto Tributario, Art. 12) subject to worldwide income taxation at the general corporate rate of 35% (Art. 240 ET, modified by Law 2277/2022). Non-resident shareholders are separately taxed on dividends at 7.5% unless treaty relief applies. No territorial limitation applies to corporate residence; branch or nominee structures are taxed only on Colombian-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia has no 'check-the-box' or pass-through election; an S.A.S. is always a separate taxable entity. Available elections and preferential regimes include: (i) optional 'Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE)' under Articles 903-916 ET, which consolidates income tax, industry-and-commerce tax (ICA), and VAT into a single payment, available only if the prior-year gross income is ≤100,000 UVT (approx. COP 4.7 billion for 2024) and natural persons hold at least 50% of the equity; (ii) the creative industries ('Economía Naranja') 7-year income tax exemption for qualifying design, software, and creative merchandising companies under Article 176 of Law 1955/2019, subject to DIAN registration and compliance with employment and export conditions; (iii) mandatory election and disclosure of hybrid mismatch arrangements and CFC attribution rules under Law 2010/2019 (Arts. 18-2 et seq. ET); and (iv) partial imputation of corporate tax to resident dividend recipients. Fiscal consolidation and partnership pass-through are not available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre las Ventas (IVA / Value Added Tax) - regulated by Articles 420-481 of the Estatuto Tributario and unified by Decree 1625 of 2016 (Title V).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No economic turnover threshold applies to legal entities: an S.A.S. is mandatorily classified as a 'Responsable del IVA' from the date of commencement of taxable activities, regardless of sales volume (Art. 437 ET). Effective registration threshold is COP 0. For reference, the optional SIMPLE regime applies to companies with prior-year gross income of up to 100,000 UVT (approx. COP 4.7 billion in 2024).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing ('Factura Electrónica de Venta - FEV') under DIAN Resolution 000165 of 2023. Each invoice must be generated in XML, signed with a certified digital certificate, carry a unique CUFE/CUDS code and QR code, and be synchronously transmitted to DIAN through the 'Sistema de Facturación Electrónica' via an approved software or technology operator. DIAN performs real-time validation and assigns acceptance/rejection status; the buyer's 'Aceptación Expresa o Tácita' event must also be reported. VAT returns are filed electronically on Form 300 through Muisca on a monthly basis. General designer toys under ISIC 3240 are not subject to special stamping regimes, but the electronic delivery document ('Documento Soporte en Adquisiciones') applies for purchases from non-invoicing suppliers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are 'Excluidos' (exempt with input-VAT refund entitlement) under Article 481 ET. Goods criteria: (i) definitive customs exportation under Decree 1165/2019; (ii) sale to a non-resident purchaser; (iii) permanent physical exit from Colombian territory. Services criteria (including software development and digital design): the beneficiary must be a non-resident without Colombian domicile; the service must be used or exploited exclusively outside Colombia; and the service must not be integrated into the Colombian recipient's productive chain. Exporters may claim monthly or bimonthly refunds of input VAT attributable to export activity by filing the VAT return (Form 300) and a 'Solicitud de Devolución' through Muisca; exporters with compliant risk profiles may access accelerated refunds under DIAN's automatic-return program.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Declaración de Exportación (DEX) - definitive export customs declaration submitted and validated through the SIGLO XXI / VUCE 'Sistema de Comercio Exterior' (Art. 274, Decree 1165/2019)
Bill of Lading (sea) or Air Waybill (air) or 'Manifiesto de Carga' (road) evidencing the physical exit of goods from Colombian territory
Inward Remittance Certificate / 'Certificado de Reintegro de Divisas' issued by a Colombian bank through the 'Formulario No. 1 - Declaración de Cambio' under the foreign exchange market rules
Commercial invoice, purchase order, and proforma invoice executed with the non-resident buyer
Certificate of origin and INVIMA/SIC technical compliance certificates for toys (domain-specific, not tax evidence)
RUT certificate showing the exporter classification and the economic activity code 3240
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN cross-verifies export VAT refunds against the SIGLO XXI customs export database, electronic invoices, and the foreign exchange track records in the SADEX system; any inconsistency in the physical exit, beneficiary, or FX repatriation results in immediate rejection of the refund claim. Fraudulent export schemes trigger: (i) mandatory restitution of the refunded amount plus moratory interest from the refund payment date (Art. 670 ET); (ii) a 160% inaccuracy penalty on the VAT amount wrongfully included in the refund (Art. 648 ET); (iii) administrative fines for failure to repatriate export proceeds - up to 5% of the non-repatriated amount, plus suspension of export privileges (Foreign Exchange Regulations, Banco de la República); and (iv) criminal liability for customs fraud and tax evasion (Law 1762/2015, Art. 434B ET) with imprisonment of 2 to 8 years for knowingly signing false export declarations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia), acting jointly with the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) and the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia for enforcement of customs, tax, and financial-prudential aspects of the Colombian foreign exchange regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso is fully convertible for current account transactions, including payments for goods, services, and operating expenses, subject to documentary requirements and clearance through authorized foreign exchange market intermediaries. Capital account transactions are generally free but require systematic registration under the foreign exchange regime, especially for foreign direct investment (FDI), because the right subsequently to repatriate capital and remit dividends is conditioned on such registration. Profit remittance requires proof of foreign investment registration, corporate financial statements, tax compliance certificates, and documentation that the funds were acquired through authorized foreign exchange channeling. No material quantitative convertibility restrictions apply, but legal entities must operate through a local authorized intermediary for proceeds from exports to be recognized as validly channeled.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Colombian foreign exchange rules, export receipts from goods such as designer toys must be channeled through an authorized Colombian foreign exchange intermediary. The statutory default timeline requires channeling within six months from the shipment date, subject to extensions available from Banco de la República depending on the payment terms. The mandatory channeling ratio is effectively 100 percent of export proceeds: the exporter must either sell the foreign currency to an authorized intermediary or deposit it in a permitted foreign-currency account maintained with such intermediary in Colombia. Retention of export proceeds abroad outside the authorized market is not permitted for routine goods exports without an express central bank exemption.

Operational Account / Foreign Currency Deposit Account
Operational Account / Foreign Currency Deposit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low as a primary or standalone banking rail; Moderate as a payment collection enabler only. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Wise, Airwallex, and Payoneer are not licensed Colombian banking institutions and cannot legally replace a local account with an authorized foreign exchange intermediary for export-proceeds channeling or statutory FDI registration. They may be used to collect e-commerce receipts, but funds must be repatriated promptly into a Colombian authorized bank account in compliance with export proceeds channeling rules. Legal constraints include prohibition on unauthorized deposit-taking in Colombia, failure to provide a Colombian NIT-based account, and possible non-recognition under DIAN reconciliation if payments are held offshore instead of being channeled through the Colombian exchange market.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Colombian corporate-account opening generally requires the legal representative to attend a KYC interview and present original identification documents. In practice, physical presence is required for non-resident directors or shareholders unless the SAS appoints a local legal representative with a properly authenticated power of attorney. Some institutions allow remote opening through biometric verification and live video interviews for resident individuals, but non-resident legal representatives must usually execute an apostilled and legalized corporate authorization. The mandated documentation includes RUT certificate, certificate of incorporation, bylaws (estatutos), proof of tax registration (NIT), UBO declaration, financial or source-of-funds information, and board/shareholder resolutions identifying the authorizing officers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial ownership with opaque structure or nominee-shareholder indicators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate structure certificate from the Colombian registry; updated UBO form with full identity and nationality declarations; organizational chart covering all shareholding levels; sworn statements from ultimate shareholders; certified passport copies; and background information explaining the commercial purpose of each entity in the ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border e-commerce payment patterns through Shopify Payments and Stripe producing fragmented micro-transactions from multiple countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant agreements with Shopify and Stripe; platform settlement reports and bank deposit evidence; itemized sales invoices and transaction log; consumer order metadata showing bona fide online sales; DIAN VAT and income tax filings aligned with declared revenue; and a reconciliation memorandum explaining typical payment frequencies and settlement delays.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Collectible and blind-box designer toy products may be preliminarily mischaracterized as gaming devices or prize/lottery instruments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC 3240 and NAICS 339930 classification certificates; product catalogs and photographs showing vinyl art collectibles; marketing materials confirming non-random, informational display of product lines; legal opinion confirming no statutory gaming license is required; and intellectual-property or copyright registration certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Upfront capital injection from offshore shareholders without an underlying trade invoice, triggering source-of-funds scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign investment registration with Banco de la República; corporate board resolution approving the capital contribution; signed shareholders agreement and share subscription documents; source-of-funds declaration supported by audited statements or bank reference letters from the remitting institution; and the SAS tax identification documentation proving the beneficiary is the registered Colombian entity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound FDI proceeds must be wired through an authorized Colombian commercial bank using SWIFT MT103 messaging from the overseas bank to the SAS account. The wire must reference the company's complete corporate name and NIT to avoid reconciliation failures. The issuing bank should state the purpose code corresponding to 'Direct Investment in Colombia' in accordance with Banco de la República's foreign exchange form methodology, generally reported by the receiving Colombian intermediary on the applicable foreign direct investment declaration form. The beneficiary account may be a COP operational account or a permitted foreign-currency deposit account. The foreign investment must be registered with Banco de la República to establish future capital repatriation and dividend remittance rights. Supporting verification includes the intervening certification from the receiving bank, source-of-funds documentation, corporate approvals, and the registered foreign investment declaration number.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments to overseas suppliers, contract manufacturers, and logistics vendors are cleared through SWIFT MT103 transfers via the same authorized commercial bank. For goods imports, the importer must present an import declaration to DIAN and channel the payment through the foreign exchange market using the applicable import goods purpose code and declaration form. For larger or credit-backed transactions, a commercial letter of credit may be opened under UCP600 or a collection arrangement accepted by the local bank, with documents such as commercial invoice, bill of lading, certificate of origin, and quality inspection certificates conforming strictly to the LC terms. Advance payments require the underlying pro-forma invoice, a supplier contract, and, where required, proof of the ordering company's inventory commitment. All outbound wires must include clear payment references, NIT verification, and the Colombian tax and customs export-import codes to ensure DIAN reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/COP forward contracts executed with authorized Colombian foreign exchange intermediaries
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/COP used for hedging economic exposure where settlement is in COP or USD outside Colombia
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) between COP and USD, including fixed-to-fixed and fixed-to-floating structures
Regulated foreign-exchange options on USD/COP for hedging contingencies and committed cash flows
Foreign-currency deposit accounts at authorized banks that enable natural FX offset and treasury pooling without speculative exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (local Chamber of Commerce of the registered office; Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá for Bogotá-domiciled entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Progressive surcharge of 10% for renewal between 1 April and 30 June, 20% between 1 July and 30 September and 30% between 1 October and 31 December, plus a storage fee surcharge; failure to renew by 31 December causes the commercial registration to be cancelled and the entity to be struck from the commercial registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (Estados Financieros) signed by legal representative and certified accountant, filed with the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio; additionally the Superintendencia de Sociedades for S.A.S. entities subject to its permanent supervision
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of the fiscal year-end, i.e. by 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines by the Superintendencia de Sociedades (generally up to 200 SMMLV for the legal representative), formal warnings and publicity of non-compliance; repeated non-filing may lead to intervention and, eventually, administrative dissolution or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting Minutes (Acta de Asamblea General Ordinaria) approving the annual financial statements and distribution results
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not routinely filed with a regulator; recorded in the statutory minute book and, when legally required, registered with the Cámara de Comercio
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Meeting must be held by 31 March of each year; minutes entered in the minute book within 30 days thereafter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of up to 200 SMMLV against the legal representative and possible intervention by the Superintendencia de Sociedades; persistent failure to hold ordinary meetings can constitute grounds for judicial dissolution of the S.A.S.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Ultimate Beneficial Owner (Confirmación Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Beneficiarios Finales reporting module annexed to the annual commercial registry renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 January and 31 March of each year, together with the commercial registry renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines imposed by the Superintendencia de Sociedades for incomplete, untruthful or late UBO filings; the annual renewal or share transfers cannot be registered until the UBO confirmation is regularized, and cancellation of the commercial registration may follow if the renewal is not completed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Auditor's Report (Dictamen del Revisor Fiscal) accompanying the annual financial statements, or registration of the revisor fiscal appointment when the audit threshold is first crossed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (with the financial statements); report also presented to the shareholders at the annual meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March for the annual financial statements; appointment registration within 30 days of the shareholders' resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Financial statements filed without the mandatory revisor fiscal report are defective; the Superintendencia de Sociedades may impose fines, require the accounts to be reprocessed, and the auditors' and shareholders' approvals may be legally challenged.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory revisor fiscal (statutory auditor) for an S.A.S. where: (1) total assets or gross income at 31 December of the preceding year exceed 5,000 SMMLV (for 2025, approximately COP 7,117,500,000, about USD 1.7 million); (2) the company is subject to the permanent inspection and supervision of the Superintendencia de Sociedades; or (3) the by-laws or the shareholders' meeting require it; below such thresholds no government-mandated independent audit applies for a private S.A.S., though voluntary audits may be agreed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian statutory accounting based on IFRS as adopted under Law 1314 of 2009 and compiled by Decreto 2420 of 2015 and Decreto 2270 of 2019; Group 1 entities apply full IFRS, typical S.A.S. entities apply IFRS for SMEs (Group 2), and micro-entities apply the simplified regulatory framework (Group 3).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual UBO confirmation is filed with the Cámara de Comercio together with the commercial registry renewal (1 January to 31 March). The legal representative must confirm and update the ultimate beneficial owner details, including identity, tax residence and direct or indirect ownership/control percentages, so the UBO file remains consistent with the shareholder ledger after any share transfers in the prior year. Each share transfer in the S.A.S. must also be entered in the Libro de Accionistas at the time it occurs, and the UBO registry is reconciled at the annual confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de Asamblea y Junta Directiva)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas)
Revisor Fiscal Book (Libro de Revisor Fiscal) where a statutory auditor is required

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 120 to USD 700 per year for registered office and/or commercial agent services in Colombia, depending on city, virtual office package and Chamber of Commerce assistance; representatives in Bogotá usually charge USD 300 to USD 600.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 1,800 to USD 6,500 for an IFRS-for-SMEs statutory audit or external review of a small designer-toy S.A.S. in Colombia; a continuing revisor fiscal engagement typically costs USD 2,000 to USD 8,000 per year.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to ISIC 3240 designer blind box toy manufacturing. General incentives include the additional 25% deduction for qualifying science, technology and innovation investments, the deduction for payroll of employees under 25 years of age, and standard statutory deductions for wages, social security, rent, and depreciable production assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 110 – Declaración de Renta y Complementarios, filed electronically through DIAN's MUISCA portal (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicios y Trámites Autónomos).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a Colombian S.A.S. with a calendar fiscal year ending 31 December, the Form 110 return is due in September of the following year, with the exact filing date assigned by DIAN based on the last two digits of the NIT. Large taxpayers may be assigned earlier dates in the annual DIAN tax calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIT, legal entity identification, business address, and primary economic activity code. The activity code must be ISIC 3240 / CIIU 3240 for designer toy manufacturing and blind box merchandising.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable; the taxpayer is the Colombian resident S.A.S. Non-resident shareholders do not sign or file the Colombian entity's Form 110.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income, including domestic and export sales of designer blind box toys, e-commerce revenue through Shopify or Stripe, and incidental licensing or merchandising income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All gross income attributable to the Colombian entity's permanent establishment and business operations must be included. Non-resident shareholders have no direct filing obligation for this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, including rotocasting resins, molds, vinyl, paint, airbrush consumables, direct labor, inbound freight, and inventory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If raw materials are imported from related non-resident suppliers, the cost line must be supported by transfer pricing documentation and arm's length pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net liquid taxable income after permitted deductions, rent exemptions, and loss carryforward offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border deductions must satisfy beneficial ownership and economic substance requirements; otherwise the DIAN may recharacterize or disallow the deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed at the statutory 35% rate, reduced by prepayments and tax prepayments made through the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No non-resident instruction; any withholding on future profit repatriation is computed separately at dividend remittance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance due or carryforward credit after comparing assessed tax against advance payments and withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a balance due exists, payment must be made in Colombian pesos via DIAN's electronic banking channels. Dividend distribution is governed by separate withholding rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a penalty equal to 5% of the income tax payable for each month or fraction of delay, capped at 100% of the tax payable. If the return shows no tax payable, the penalty is calculated at 0.5% of gross income, subject to minimum fixed amounts. Unpaid balances accrue monthly default interest at the DIAN rate (approximately 1.2% per month). False or inexact returns may attract the inaccuracy penalty equal to 100% of the tax difference, plus criminal exposure if fraud is established.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders from profits that have already been subject to Colombian corporate income tax. Dividends distributed from untaxed or exempt profits are subject to a 35% final withholding tax when remitted to non-residents, unless a treaty provides a lower rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double tax agreement (DTA) dividend rate, the non-resident shareholder must provide the Colombian S.A.S. with the following before payment: (i) an official Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction for the calendar year of payment; (ii) a signed Beneficial Ownership Declaration confirming entitlement to treaty benefits; and (iii) documentary evidence of share ownership. The withholding agent applies the reduced rate only if the documentation is received before the dividend payment. If excess withholding occurs, the shareholder may claim a refund from DIAN within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 20% withholding on IP royalties and technical service payments, and 20% withholding on debt interest paid to non-residents. Under Colombia's DTA network, the treaty rate is commonly reduced to 10% or 15% for royalties and 10% or 15% for interest, subject to beneficial ownership and limitation-of-benefits clauses. Payments to related parties in zero-tax or no-tax jurisdictions may be recharacterized, non-deductible, and subject to an additional 35% remittance tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File (Informe Local) is mandatory when the taxpayer's gross income or total assets equal or exceed 100,000 UVT (approximately COP 4.7 billion for tax year 2024). Master File (Informe Maestro) filing is triggered when the multinational group's consolidated revenue equals or exceeds 300,000 UVT (approximately COP 14.1 billion). Documentation must be filed electronically through the DIAN TP portal; late or incomplete filings carry separate sanctions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not apply a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime, but the DIAN applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR), substance-over-form jurisprudence, and beneficial ownership requirements. An S.A.S. engaged in designer blind box manufacturing must demonstrate real business activity through premises, employees, inventory, production equipment, and actual risk assumption. Shell structures that merely invoice merchandise or royalties through a Colombian entity without operational substance will be denied treaty relief and may face recharacterization or veil piercing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting cash or e-commerce sales of designer blind boxes from Form 110, forging supplier invoices, inflating production costs, or hiding offshore payment rails. Understating ISIC 3240 gross revenue to reduce the 35% corporate income tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN reassessment plus the 100% inaccuracy penalty (sanción por inexactitud) on the understated tax, monthly default interest, and criminal prosecution for tax evasion under Article 434A of the Colombian Criminal Code with imprisonment of 4 to 9 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties. IThe DIAN may impose travel bans, asset embargoes, and criminal arrest warrants. A fraud conviction carries disqualification from managing commercial entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the S.A.S. as a letterbox entity to book royalties, distribution margins, or holding-company income without Colombian employees, office, warehouse, production equipment, or business decisions. The entity exercises no real control over the blind box manufacturing value chain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN applies the GAAR to disregard the entity, deny treaty benefits, recharacterize transactions, and assess tax at the owner level. Penalties for abusive tax schemes can reach 50,000 UVT (approximately COP 2.35 billion) in addition to back taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Article 42 of Law 1258 of 2008 (S.A.S. regime), the corporate veil is pierced where the company is used for fraud, tax evasion, or asset stripping. Shareholders and directors become jointly liable with their personal assets for all tax liabilities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting significant cash or POS payments from repeatedly unidentified buyers, allowing the use of blind box e-commerce sales as a value-transfer mechanism, failing to perform customer due diligence on wholesale distributors, and omitting Unusual Transaction Reports (RUT) to the UIAF.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines imposed by the UIAF and Superintendencia de Sociedades of up to COP 1.5 billion; criminal money-laundering sanctions under Article 323 of Law 599 of 2000 carry imprisonment of 10 to 20 years and fines of up to 50,000 legal monthly minimum wages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers, compliance officers, and natural-person shareholders who knowingly direct or tolerate illicit fund flows face personal criminal indictment. The DIAN and Fiscalía may order asset freezing, travel bans, and extradition where applicable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation and Arm's Length Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the Informe Local and Informe Maestro, or setting non-arm's length prices for imports of vinyl pellets, rotocasting molds, resin, or design IP from related non-resident entities. Also includes failure to submit the annual transfer pricing return forms to DIAN.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN adjusts taxable income under the arm's length standard, imposes a penalty equal to 5% of the aggregate related-party transaction value (not to exceed 20,000 UVT, approximately COP 941 million), and charges monthly default interest on the resulting tax deficiency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and tax officers who sign the TP return without adequate documentation are jointly liable for the adjustment and penalty. Deliberate price manipulation with intent to evade tax is criminally prosecutable under the tax evasion article, with imprisonment and disqualification from board positions.
